editorial:
Imagine taking one of the biggest sex symbols of the seventies and pairing her with giant, colorful puppets. That is exactly what you get here. You follow Raquel Welch as she leads a wild variety show that feels like a fever dream from a 1970s dinner club. It is a strange mix of glitzy music numbers and silly comedy sketches, all brought to life by the creative minds behind the Krofft puppets. The whole vibe is bright, loud, and completely over-the-top, making you feel like you are sitting front row at a Vegas show from forty years ago.

What really works is how Raquel handles the absurdity of the show with a big smile and great energy. The pacing is quick, though some of the puppet bits might feel a bit too weird for some people. If you love vintage camp and flashy costumes, you will have a blast. Since this is an older TV special, you should look for a high-quality digital restore if possible. If you can find it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or rent it on Apple TV, it really makes those neon colors pop. Otherwise, grabbing a physical Blu-ray for your collection is the way to go.
endingExplained: The show wraps up with a huge, high-energy musical finale where Raquel and all the puppets join together on stage. There is no big plot twist because it is a variety special, but it ends on a high note with a lot of dancing and cheering. You see Raquel take a final bow as the curtain closes, leaving you with a feeling of pure 70s glamour and goofy fun.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 70s nostalgia and weird variety shows.
